source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The property of living organisms that is regarded as the most unique and defining is
questions.explanation: Consciousness (self-awareness and response to stimuli at the organism level) is treated as the defining feature of living beings.

questions.stem: Classification of animals is essential mainly because it
options: reduces the number of species on Earth
helps study the enormous diversity in an orderly way
replaces the need for scientific names
questions.explanation: Millions of species cannot be studied one by one; grouping by characters makes identification and comparison possible.

questions.stem: The branch that includes identification, nomenclature and classification of organisms is
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the practice of identifying, naming and classifying organisms.

questions.stem: In animals, related families are grouped together into a
questions.explanation: The hierarchy is species → genus → family → order → class → phylum → kingdom.

questions.stem: The basic unit used in the classification of animals is the
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest and fundamental unit of taxonomic classification.

questions.stem: In the scientific name Panthera leo, the word Panthera stands for the
questions.explanation: The first word of a binomial is the genus; leo is the specific epithet of the lion.

questions.stem: Scientific names of animals are framed according to the
questions.explanation: The International Code of Zoological Nomenclature governs animal names; plants follow ICN.

questions.stem: Living wild animals kept for public education and study are maintained in a
questions.explanation: Zoological parks (zoos) house living animals; museums store preserved specimens.

questions.stem: A taxonomic monograph differs from a flora because a monograph
options: gives a comprehensive account of a single taxon
identifies plants solely by flower colour
questions.explanation: A monograph treats one taxon in depth; a flora catalogues plants of a region.

questions.stem: In print, the two words of an animal's binomial should appear in
questions.explanation: Printed scientific names are italicised; the genus starts with a capital letter.

questions.stem: Isolated enzyme reactions in a test tube are not considered living because they lack
questions.explanation: Metabolism of life occurs inside organised cells; a cell-free mixture is not an organism.

questions.stem: Among class, order, family and genus of animals, the rank that is immediately above family is
questions.explanation: Ascending order: genus → family → order → class.

questions.stem: Which statement about the name Homo sapiens is incorrect?
options: Homo is the genus and is capitalised
sapiens is the specific epithet and is not capitalised
Both words together denote the species
sapiens alone is a valid name of the species
questions.explanation: A species name is binomial; the specific epithet sapiens is not used alone as a scientific name.

questions.stem: Growth by accumulation of material on the surface can occur in mountains. Living growth differs because it is
questions.explanation: Living organisms grow by internal cell division, not by external deposition.

questions.stem: The known number of animal species is far larger than that of plants. This fact mainly emphasises the need for
options: a standardised system of classification and naming
placing all animals in one genus
questions.explanation: Great diversity requires agreed names and hierarchical grouping so species can be identified worldwide.

questions.stem: Systematics is broader than taxonomy because it also considers
options: only the economic value of animals
questions.explanation: Systematics includes phylogeny in addition to identification, naming and classification.

questions.stem: Which taxonomic category of animals includes all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Phylum is the highest of these ranks and contains many classes, orders, families and genera.

questions.stem: Two animals that can interbreed in nature and produce fertile young belong to the same
options: genus only if they look identical
questions.explanation: The biological species concept groups organisms that actually or potentially interbreed and yield fertile offspring.

questions.stem: Linnaeus established the practice of naming each organism with
options: two Latinised words, genus and specific epithet
the family name followed by a number
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature uses Genus + specific epithet as the scientific name.

questions.stem: ICZN does not apply to the naming of
questions.explanation: Animal names follow ICZN; plant names follow the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants.

questions.stem: Preserved skins, skeletons and stuffed animals used as taxonomic references are stored in a
questions.explanation: Museums keep dead, preserved animal specimens; zoos keep living animals.

questions.stem: A dichotomous taxonomic key identifies an unknown animal by
questions.explanation: Each couplet offers two opposite choices that lead to the next step or the name.

questions.stem: When handwritten, each of the two words of a binomial should be
questions.explanation: Handwritten scientific names are underlined separately in place of italics.

questions.stem: Reproduction cannot be treated as an exclusive defining feature of living organisms because
options: many organisms such as mules and sterile worker bees do not reproduce
questions.explanation: Infertile organisms are still living; some non-living systems can also 'multiply' in a trivial sense.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pairing of rank and example.
questions.explanation: leo is a specific epithet, not a class. Lion: genus Panthera, family Felidae, order Carnivora, class Mammalia.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a taxonomic aid used in zoology?
questions.explanation: Museums, zoos and keys help identification; a spectrophotometer is a laboratory instrument, not a taxonomic aid.
